To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a method for measuring metallicities of globular clusters using HST/WFC photometry, and that this method is accurate to ~0.1-0.5 dex in [Fe/Fe], depending on the filter set.

we calibrated the metallicities of stellar populations using the F555W-F814w color and the Dartmouth isocrones, and that we tested and calibrated the metal and temperature sensitivity of the F390M-F390W and the F390W-F390M colors using the same isochrone grid and stellar models.
the WFC3 photometry is sensitive to metallicity and that the photometric metallicity can be determined to an accuracy of ~ 0.2-0.5 dex for stellar populations with a range of metallicities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of the WFC3 filters to measure the metallicities of stellar populations in distant galaxies.
the calibration of the WFC3 photometric metallicity measurements and the accuracy of these measurements in the context of measuring stellar metallicities of globular clusters.
the calibration and accuracy of the WFC3/UVIS photometry to measure the metallicity of unresolved stellar populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the (F390M - F555W) vs. (F555W - F814W) diagram is the best suited to recover photometric metallicities with HST photometry.
F390M-F390W is the most reliable color-color diagram for determining the metallicities of globular clusters.
the F390M-F390W-F555F-WFC3 color-color diagram is the best choice for measuring photometric metallicities from stellar clusters, with F390W--F555F-WFC as a good second choice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the (F390M--F555W,F814W) color-color diagram is best suited to measure metallicities of stellar populations, and that this diagram is the most efficient and accurate way to measure photometric metallicity using the WFC3/UVIS camera.

the (F390M -F555W, F555W-F814) color-color diagram, with the empirical calibration we present, is the best suited to determine the metallicities of stellar populations with the WFC3/UVIS camera aboard the Hubble space telescope.
we can measure the metallicity of a stellar cluster using HST photometry to ~0.1 - 0.3 dex when the cluster age, distance, and reddening are approximately known.
The main takeaway from our work is that
WFC3 photometry can be used to measure photometric metallicity of globular clusters and young star clusters to ~0.1 - 0.2 dex.
photometric metallicity estimates are possible for clusters with unknown age and metal content using the F390M and F390W filters.

the F390M-F390W color-color diagram is the best suited for measuring photometric metallicities with WFC3 photometry, and that this method can be used to measure the metallicities of globular clusters and young star clusters in the Local Group and beyond.
